title: Getting realistic cue-ball spin out of Claude Code (Opus 5.5, high effort) for a browser pool and snooker game
author: vinishkapoor
selftext:
I wanted to see how far an AI coding agent could get with cue sports physics, since that’s where a pool game usually feels fake. I used Claude Code with Opus 5.5 on high effort.

**Workflow that worked:**

1. **Physics before rules.** I started with only a table and a few balls, so every round of feedback was about ball movement.
2. **Describe the feel.** “Low hit should pull back further” or “side spin should change the angle off the cushion” got better results than vague asks. It took a lot of rounds.
3. **Small realism details next.** Jaw rattle on a near miss and a pocket sound added more than I expected.
4. **One rule set at a time.** I did 8-Ball first, then Snooker, which was the hardest because of re-spotting and the order of colours at the end, then a two-minute Blitz mode.
5. **AI opponent last.** Three levels. The main fix was making it pick makeable shots instead of the nearest ball.

It runs in the browser on desktop and mobile, with no sign-up:  
[https://vinish.dev/velvet-break-pool-snooker-browser-based-game](https://vinish.dev/velvet-break-pool-snooker-browser-based-game)

If you’ve made physics-heavy games with AI, I’m curious what worked for you.
